rv.q: The closer you examine it, the less moving it becomes.
While the play's dual timeline structure is cleverly conceived, the execution is uneven, with stronger scenes set in the present than those depicting Monet's struggles.
'Impressionism' is an elaborate if awkward romance _ positively brimming with self-importance.

But I’ve concluded that even if I were to back up all the way to the Hudson River, with half-open eyes fixed on the stage where Mr. Irons and Ms. Allen labor so valiantly, “Impressionism” still wouldn’t look credible.
'Impressionism' manages what would seem to be impossible. It makes bores out of two unconscionably attractive and intelligent actors.
Both lead actors seem stumped by their awkwardly, sentimentally drawn roles, as does their estimable director, Jack O'Brien.
The play suffers from three major ailments: pretentiousness, trickery and triviality.
With Impressionism , 100 intermissionless minutes seem like endless hours.

Even the talented Jeremy Irons and Joan Allen and director Jack O'Brien, who have five Tonys among them, aren't able to breathe charm or art into this pale drama by Michael Jacobs, which is both obscure and simplistic.
Despite a solid cast headed by Jeremy Irons, Joan Allen and Marsha Mason, this new American play by Michael Jacobs too often feels like an art history quiz.
